voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: The South Atlantic, December nineteen twenty-eight. The København, then the largest sailing ship in the world, left Buenos Aires for Australia.
Sixty people were aboard. Forty-five were cadets, most of them teenagers.
Eight days out, she radioed a passing steamer that all was well. When it called her again, she did not answer.
A search across the South Atlantic lasted months. Reported sightings followed. None was ever confirmed.
No one aboard was ever seen again. Nearly a century later, no wreck has ever been confirmed.
